qt: to the Commission Sander Smit (ECR) Subject:

The Netherlands submitted its draft restoration plan on 25 August 2026 via Reportnet; the submission is restricted, whilst Sweden’s submission was made public1. In its answer to written question E-001684/20262, the Commission confirmed that its comments under Article 17 would be made public and emphasised transparent preparation and public consultation. A six-week public consultation on a public version of the draft has been announced for October; the plan’s environmental impact assessment will follow in the autumn. A previous formal public consultation concerned the methodology of the environmental impact assessment. 1.

On what grounds is the Dutch submission restricted, and will the Commission, or the EEA as the relevant authority, make the submitted draft, together with its annexes and amended versions, available to the public upon request pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 and Regulation (EC) No 1367/2006, having regard to Article 6(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1367/2006?
What type of public participation and justification are required under Article 14(20) and Article 15(3)(w) prior to submission?

In accordance with Article 17, what consequences does the Commission attach to the absence of information on public participation or to discrepancies between the version submitted and the version made available for inspection, and what additional consultation or renewed public participation is required prior to the adoption of the final plan?

at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.11.2026) The Nature Restoration Regulation (NRR)1 requires final nature restoration plans to be published. Whether the draft plans submitted to the Commission are made public2 is for Member States to decide. The Commission has strongly encouraged publication of drafts, in line with national procedures and the NRR public participation requirements. If the Commission receives an access to documents request, it will apply the relevant rules, in particular as set out in Regulation (EC) 1049/20013. Under Article 14(20), Member States must ensure that preparation of national restoration plans is open, transparent, inclusive and effective, and that the public and relevant stakeholders have early and effective opportunities to participate. Detailed arrangements are set by Member States in accordance with rules under the Aarhus Convention4, secondary law5, as well as under national law. Public participation processes must take place during preparation of drafts prior to their submission, and may continue after submission of the draft if national rules provide so. Under Article 15(3)(w), national restoration plans must summarise the preparation process, including public participation and how local communities’ and stakeholders’ needs were considered. This may include information on the type, number and organisers of public participation activities, communication channels and methods, the process for identifying stakeholders and sectors involved, the timing and length of consultations, the feedback received and how it was reflected in the plan. Compliance with this obligation will be evaluated by the Commission as part of its assessment of draft national restoration plans under Article 17(2)a.
